perspective:
Harold Padilla’s available information:

- He is a Project Manager and knows his own feelings, thoughts, intentions, and actions.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a police officer and trusted friend/advisor he can rely on for support.
- In the coffee-shop meeting, Harold feels frustrated and anxious that his project team is unmotivated and affecting progress. He tells Arthur this. He hears Arthur advise understanding each team member’s individual motivation and trying one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood. Harold says he had focused on goals/deadlines, agrees to try the advice, thanks Arthur, and feels hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold tells his team he wants one-on-one chats to understand what motivates them. He hears Team Member 1 say that could help and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. He says he will schedule time and asks the team to work together for success.
- Later, Harold notices the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried. He tells Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still is not responding. He hears Arthur suggest deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold says he had not thought of that, asks what issues Arthur means, thanks him, and decides to hold another round of meetings.
- In one-on-one meetings, Harold tells team members he noticed performance issues and asks about concerns. He hears Team Member 1 say there is tension among a few team members affecting work. He hears Team Member 2 say they feel overwhelmed by workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts and consider redistributing tasks, and that their well-being is important.
- In a final team meeting, Harold feels optimistic and empowered. He tells the team he heard their concerns and will implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a supportive environment. He hears Team Member 1 say that sounds great and should help, and Team Member 2 agree that it is good their concerns are being addressed. Harold says he is glad and asks the team to work together, saying their input and well-being are crucial.
